why: XLC -4.36 pct to $105.51, its lowest close since Jul 23 and 48 cents over the 52-week closing low; Wednesday's $108.97 broke the $109.66 floor on the week's heaviest volume (wiki/communication-services.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 2; macro/facts.json).

Both ends of the barbell fell: Meta -9.4 pct on capex passing operating cash flow (FCF -$2.1B), Netflix -6.6 pct on a Q4 guide and ad cut, and the SpaceX ~80,000-tower report took AT&T -10.7 pct on the week and TMUS to a two-year low (wiki/communication-services.md; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 1 and Wire 4).

Week RF cut 35 -> 30 and MC 38 -> 40: GOOGL and TMUS report Wed Oct 28 and VZ Mon, a binary set on a fund whose platforms are graded on cash, not budgets (wiki/earnings-surveillance.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 4).
risks: Alphabet showing capex covered by cash flow answers the 'who pays' question on an oversold fund 48 cents above its low; Marky's short covers a third at $105.03 and a close over $109.66 invalidates the call (wiki/synthesis.md Section 4 and Section 5).
A SpaceX denial or VZ/TMUS commentary that no tower deal exists reverses Friday's carrier selling (wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.B.5).

why: XLC is 6.50 pts behind SPY over a month and below both its 50-day and 200-day; correlation to SPY 0.440 on Canary's 30-day window (wiki/synthesis.md Section 3; wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX).

Ophelia moved platforms and telecom to underweight until cash covers capex; the ad forecast cut at Netflix and the SpaceX entry into towers both hit the fund's two halves (wiki/communication-services.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.B.2).
risks: The fund is concentrated (platforms ~43 pct, weights approximate): one hyperscaler print that shows cash flow can re-rate it within the month (wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.C; wiki/communication-services.md).
Cecil buys TMUS at 10.2x with 62 pct to target; a clean Oct 28 print would make the telecom selloff the value entry he calls it (wiki/synthesis.md Section 1).

extracts.lead_summary: The coil broke, and it broke down. XLC closed $105.51, -4.4%, its lowest close since July 23 and 48 cents above the 52-week closing low. Both ends of the barbell fell in the same week. The platforms fell on their own prints: Meta beat on revenue and still lost 7% Thursday on a $9.9B legal charge and capex that outran operating cash flow; Netflix beat on earnings, guided Q4 below and cut its ad forecast, and lost 5% Wednesday. Alphabet fell 6% without reporting. Then on Friday Bloomberg reported SpaceX in talks for about 80,000 tower sites, and the carriers fell again: AT&T -8.0% on the day, -10.7% on the week after a beat-and-raise; T-Mobile to its lowest close in two years. Comcast and Disney rose. The hedge stopped hedging.
